title: FPT approximation of twin-width
formal: Do there exist total computable functions \(f,g:N\to N\) and a constant \(c\ge 1\), and one deterministic Turing machine A, such that for every finite nonempty simple graph G on n vertices and integer \(k\ge 0, A\) halts within \(f(k)(n+1)^{c}\) bit operations and either correctly reports \(tww(G)>k\) or outputs a contraction sequence of G of width at most \(g(k)\)? No order, decomposition or contraction sequence is supplied with G.
definitions: The input gives n, the \(n\times n\) adjacency matrix of G, and k in binary. A contraction sequence is a sequence of partitions of \(V(G)\), starting with the singleton partition and ending with \(\{V(G)\}\), each obtained from its predecessor by merging two parts. For distinct parts X,Y, their pair is mixed if there exist both an adjacent pair \(x\in X,y\in Y\) and a nonadjacent pair \(x' \in X,y' \in Y\) in the original graph. The red degree of a part is the number of other parts with which it has a mixed pair. The sequence width is the maximum red degree over every part of every partition. Twin-width \(tww(G)\) is the minimum sequence width; a one-vertex graph has twin-width zero. The output lists the \(n- 1\) merges using integer part labels. Both f and g depend only on k, whereas c is independent of k and G. If \(tww(G)\le k\), rejection is forbidden. If \(tww(G)>k\), either a correct rejection or the stated bounded-width sequence is allowed.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine whether the structural certificates behind twin-width algorithms can be found efficiently from an unordered graph.

importance.reason: A central algorithmic access problem for a major graph-width parameter, with consequences for the applicability of logical algorithms on bounded twin-width classes.

progress.text: The twin-width-one recognition paper still describes general XP approximation, and therefore FPT approximation, as open.

context_blocks.text: Twin-width measures how many mixed adjacency relations arise while vertices are progressively grouped. A graph may possess a low-width sequence even when finding that sequence from its ordinary representation is difficult.

The research-project question asks for fixed-parameter approximation with arbitrary computable width loss. It is therefore more basic than obtaining a particular approximation ratio: even a very large output-width function depending only on k would answer it.

Recognition and structural descriptions at twin-width one are established special cases. Approximation procedures for ordered structures receive additional information that this input does not contain. Neither result supplies the requested general algorithm.

sentences: Twin-width measures mixed adjacency during repeated merges of vertex groups.
The question asks for an algorithm that finds a bounded-width merge sequence whenever the graph has twin-width at most k.
Its running time may depend arbitrarily on k but only polynomially on graph size, with an exponent independent of k.
The algorithm receives the graph alone, without a useful vertex order or decomposition.
A positive answer would make twin-width-based algorithmic methods accessible from ordinary graph input.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. Bonnet lists the FPT approximation question, and the 2025 recognition paper explicitly leaves even general XP approximation open. No general resolution was found in the same-day review.

notes: Expanded the standard rejection-or-decomposition definition of parameterized approximation and defined red degree directly through partitions.
statement_review.scope: Individual mathematical formulation and source review; not a proof-assistant formalization or verification of the cited proofs.

review_note: Distinct from TCS-0342 on string-graph twin-width and TCS-7181 on exact clique-width. The current and historical review found no duplicate. Expanded the standard rejection-or-decomposition definition of parameterized approximation and defined red degree directly through partitions.
